newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Mar 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Editorials-Mar 17.

text.p: - There are 106 days to go before the British colony reverts to China. These are highlights of comments in the Hong Kong press. The views expressed are those of the newspapers quoted and do not represent an editorial viewpoint of Reuters.

-- The Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO said the British side had no right to monitor the operation of the post-handover Special Administrative Region government. It said that Governor Chris Patten was trying to mislead the public by saying that the Joint Liaison Group would exist until the year 2000.

-- APPLE DAILY said that if China was confident that the "one country, two systems" principle could be carried out properly after the handover, it should not be afraid of criticism. It said the Chinese government could show its respect for international laws by inviting the international community to watch how Hong Kong would operate in the future.

-- The HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL said the speech by the head of China's National People's Congress revealed some serious problems in China. It said the newly-passed National Defence Law, which says the army should be led by the Communist Party, contradicts the Constitution which says that the army should be under the leadership of the People's Republic. The paper said this revealed that most senior Chinese leaders lacked legal sense and tended to legalise the wishes of some Party leaders.
